newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks soar to record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks soar to record close.

text.p: *Stocks smash way to record highs and record close, miners, banks lead way up as investors jump in. Volume 527.90 million, value A$1.32 bln, 1,157 stocks traded, 288 steady, 586 up, 283 down.
Traders said the cocktail of stronger metals prices, growth prospects of the yield-rich big banks and a soaring Wall Street had proved to be a heady mix for enthusiastic investors.
"It's been a very exciting day and we've seen some big money come into the market," said Greg Matthews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual Investment Management.
"Banks had a great day, the golds and metals companies are up, clearly on the back of stronger metal prices overseas and the Dow is up. Everything has come together today."
National Australia Bank led the booming bank sector higher, jumping 2.8 percent to close at A$16.52.
The big banks climbed to record highs early before all except National Australia Bank succumbed to profit taking near their fresh tops.
The major miners were firmer across the board, the gold sector impressing with a 1.9 percent jump.

Shares in property developer/financial services group Lend Lease Corp jumped higher early after a 14.2 percent higher first half net profit of A$160 million but ended 11 cents lower at A$23.00. Brokers said the strong price rise had proved too tempting for some with the result failing to convince others.
It was a big day for media stocks results.

Prime Television shares closed five censt higher at A$2.55 after a 21.6 percent higher first half net profit of A$7.98 million. Rural Press reported a four percent higher first half net profit of A$16.96 million after trading closed. Its shares had ended at A$4.10, steady on the day.
PMP Communications unchanged after its 2.6 percent lower first half net profit of A$30.55 million.
In the resources, results came from contract miner Eltin whose shares ended eight cents higher at A$2.73 after a more than doubled first half net profit.
Placer Dome's 77 percent owned Placer Pacific reported a full year net profit of A$43.2 million, its shares closing four cents higher at A$1.78.

Media giant News Corp shared in the market's good cheer early but retreated to end lower. Traders said the focus of the day was elsewhere with a soft result from its 40.4 percent owned PMP Communications also failing to assist.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 24.9 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trading boomed in line with the active mood of the underlying markets.
Total options traded 48,106 (35,507). Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 11,220 (11,214)

In other local markets, Australian debt futures pared the sharp falls that followed strong employment data, although any glimmer of hope that a monetary policy easing was still on the cards was virtually put to rest. By 5.20 p.m (0620 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.37 percent.

The Australian dollar ended a two month slide with a one cent rally as signs of economic recovery eclipsed all thoughts of a rate cut. By 5.20 p.m. (0620 GMT) the dollar was at US$0.7675/80 from an early US$0.7595/00.
